newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga makes new gas/condensate find in Norwegian Se.
newsitem.headline: Saga makes new gas/condensate find in Norwegian Se.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA, as operator of licence 199, has made a new gas/condensate find in block 6406/2, southwest of the Smoerbukk field in the Norwegian Sea, the Oil Directorate said on Thursday.

The discovery is the second find in the block over the past year, the directorate said. No production test had been carried out and no immediate information was available on the size of the reservoir.
The Smoerbukk field forms part of the Aasgard development, which also comprises Smoerbukk South and Midgard fields.
The northern part of the discovery reaches into licence 134 in block 6506/11.
The directorate said well 6406/2-3 had reached a depth of 4,900 metres below the sea bed and would be drilled to 5,400 metres.
Partners in licence 199 are Saga with 25 percent, Mobil with 15 percent, Den norske stats oljeselskap and the government's direct financial interest (SDOE) 45 percent.
Partners in licence 134 are Statoil as operator with 28 percent, Agip with 30 percent, Saga with seven percent, Total with 10 percent and SDOE with 25 percent.
